methodology.rule_1: every count is a real response of this run; no estimation, interpolation or back-fill
methodology.rule_2: confirmed = official_id / exact_alias / multi_field from identity.CompanyIndex.resolve; candidate counted apart
methodology.rule_3: a server-side count is labelled as such and its truncation is reported as a residual
methodology.rule_4: report counts are never converted to failure/incidence rates

notes: Recall and MAUDE annual series are server-side count aggregations over the whole matched set; the identity census resolves the API's own exact-value buckets, so both counts describe the same query.

GE HealthCare: recall uses two mutually exclusive firm-string queries ('GE HEALTHCARE', 'GE MEDICAL'); the MAUDE census uses the 'ge healthcare' phrase only and therefore excludes legacy 'GE MEDICAL' manufacturer strings (documented, not estimated).

Dräger: openFDA rejects non-ASCII search terms (recalling_firm:dräger -> HTTP 400 'Search not supported'), so only the ASCII spellings draeger/drager are retrievable. The 'drager' recall query returned HTTP 404 'No matches found' (zero records) at build time — recorded, not hidden.
MAUDE keyword-family totals are report counts for reports in which at least one device entry matches the manufacturer keyword; they are not mutually exclusive across firms and carry no denominator.
fda_device_shortages: only the discontinuance table has a manufacturer column, so the shortage list itself is not firm-linkable; both counts are reported as constructed.
fda_import_alerts: firm-level coverage is UNKNOWN because the index exposes no company column.

fda_device_shortages.interpretation: The FDA shortage/discontinuance lists are point-in-time snapshots of the current list. The page is not an archive: entries disappear when resolved and earlier states are not queryable, so a short current list is not evidence that shortages were absent historically.

openfda_device_maude.interpretation: PASSIVE REPORTING COUNT, NOT AN INCIDENCE RATE. Postmarket report counts are driven by reporting incentives, litigation, media attention, product usage volume and FDA collection efforts. Increases can reflect better reporting rather than worse product quality. Never interpret a count (or a change in a count) as a failure rate, a defect rate, or evidence of quality deterioration. MAUDE only contains reports that someone chose to submit; it has no denominator of devices in use, and openFDA states that incidence cannot be determined from it.
openfda_device_maude.retrieval_mode: server-side count aggregation for the firm keyword family (report counts by date), plus a 100-bucket exact-manufacturer census for identity resolution

openfda_device_recall.interpretation: A recall record documents one enforcement action, not the underlying failure rate of a device family. Recall publication lags the initiating event and FDA does not update the status after classification; a terminated status is not evidence that the product was safe. A recall count is also not a device reliability metric: FDA seeks publicity selectively and firms self-report corrective actions.
openfda_device_recall.retrieval_mode: server-side count aggregation: exact recalling_firm census for identity resolution plus daily event/posted date buckets for the annual series
